question: A shopkeeper sold {{1} over 4} of his stock at a gain of 25%, and the remaining stock at a gain of 19%. His total percentage of gain was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick __** (SP)/(CP) = ((1×125)+(3×119))/(4×100) = 482 over 400 

⇒ Profit % = (482-400)/(400) x 100

⇒ Profit % = 20.5%

∴ Profit is 20.5%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given: **

(1/4)th of the stock is sold at 20% gain

The remaining stock is sold at 19% gain

**Formula used:**

SP = CP x (100 + Profit%)/100

**Calculation:**

Let the total stock be 400 units

CP of 400 units = ₹400

According to the question,

Total SP = 100 times (125)/(100) + 300 times (119)/(100) 

⇒ Total SP = ₹482

Profit % = (482 - 400)/400 x 100

⇒ Profit % = 20.5%

**∴ Profit is 20.5%.**
